claims.harm: Encapsulating CTransaction and removing const member variables risks mutability footguns and introduces broad churn across consensus-critical code for no immediate benefit.
claims.quote: This doesn't seem like a good idea at all to me. If you want an object that can represent different transactions over its lifetime, you should be using CMutableTransaction

claims.harm: As long as CTransactionRef shares the CTransaction wrapper, allowing assignment leaves a potential non-const alias footgun.
claims.quote: As long as CTransactionRef shares the CTransaction wrapper, making that wrapper assignable leaves a possible non-const-alias footgun.
claims.settled_by_quote: Thanks for taking the suggestions regarding removing the assignment operator, and removing the default move constructor.

claims.harm: Default move constructor on non-const members could memberwise move vin/vout vectors and leave invalid cached witness/hash fields on the moved-from instance.
claims.quote: vin/vout, being vectors, move could actually mean move the underlying storage. In light of that, I think we should delete the move constructer during the transition.
claims.settled_by_quote: Thanks for taking the suggestions regarding removing the assignment operator, and removing the default move constructor.

claims.harm: Accessor methods returning references without LIFETIMEBOUND attribute can lead to dangling reference bugs.
claims.quote: In any case, I think `LIFETIMEBOUND` could be added here?

claims.harm: Renaming well-established protocol-level names like vin and vout to GetInputs and GetOutputs creates confusion between internal Core code and external RPC/protocol terms.
claims.quote: On a language level, terms such as vin, vout etc. have long become part of the public protocol: For example encapsulating vin through GetInputs() internally within bitcoin core, just to expose them as vin again to the outside via RPC (getrawtransaction) seems weird to me

claims.harm: Massive call-site refactor in critical code without clear immediate benefit, adding duplicate accessors to CMutableTransaction to paper over generic code.
claims.quote: Approach NACK for now. I don't see a concrete benefit here that justifies rewriting so many transaction call sites in consensus, policy, mempool, wallet, tests, fuzzers, and kernel-facing code.

claims.harm: Hardcoded scaffolding clang-tidy check left in the tree adds maintenance baggage if not reusable.
claims.quote: After the final commit, the compiler enforces the CTransaction boundary, so this check is only scaffolding unless we plan to keep using it for other classes.
claims.settled_by_quote: This is an amazing use of bitcoin-tidy. Nice work getting the attribute/annotation machinery working.

support.reason: Moving data members behind observers rather than letting class layout define the API is a solid improvement towards regular value handles over immutable data.
Supports encapsulation and moving towards an immutable handle body approach.
Adding observer functions moves towards an overall better design where callers do not depend on class layout, separating serialization and transaction API from concrete layout.
Does not see practical downsides worth blocking over, and finds the techniques and direction valuable.
Verified the clang-tidy fixup reproduces cleanly (86 files modified, byte-identical or minor diffs in object files), full unit and functional tests pass.

result.notes: Initial record for PR #35569.
